subject: Realtime streams stalling under burst — ClarifyHealth production impact
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@clarityhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clarityhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream timeouts / production stalls

Diego —

We started seeing recurrent stalls on our realtime inference streams this morning around 08:45 PST. Clients report long pauses (15–45s) where no tokens are delivered, then a sudden burst of tokens. This is affecting our telehealth transcription pipeline; three sessions dropped yesterday.

Sample request IDs: req-44a3, req-44f9, req-4521. Attached is a pcap from one of the affected instances (clarity_pcap_20261122.pcap).

Logs show repeated: "websocket: read timeout after 30s" and chunked-transfer errors like "unexpected EOF while reading chunk". Latency and error rate spike during 10:00–10:30 window (we're on us-west region).

This is high priority for us — can you confirm root cause and ETA for mitigation? We need immediate mitigations and an exec update.

—Miguel
Senior Platform Engineer
ClarifyHealth
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T09:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream timeouts / production stalls

Miguel — thanks for the data and the pcap. I'm escalating this to our oncall and engineering leads immediately. Acknowledged the impact and we're treating this as a Sev1 (possible regression in chunked transfer handling under bursty traffic).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether you had any recent model variant/quantization changes pushed at ~07:30 PST?
- We'll need any client-side keepalive/heartbeat values you set (to check for mismatches).

Short-term mitigation we're going to try in parallel (will coordinate with you):
1) Increase websocket read timeout on edge proxies to 90s and enable 10s application-level heartbeat.
2) Temporarily route traffic to a fallback model variant with lower peak memory (will be no config change on your side).
3) Collect additional perf snapshots at 1m granularity; drop in our perf_snapshot_20261122.json to the shared drive.

I'll coordinate a short war room — can you confirm availability for a 10:00 PST sync?

Diego
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lauren — FYI: ClarifyHealth is asking for an exec update; we should prepare a 1‑pager with impact, mitigation, and ETA. I'll start drafting.

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime stream timeouts / production stalls

Thanks Hannah — initial triage notes below after looking at the pcap and edge logs:

Findings:
- We see frequent TCP FIN/RST sequences coinciding with websocket read-timeouts. The edge proxy (v2.14.1) is closing idle connections after 30s when chunk frames pause.
- Chunked responses from the model backend occasionally pause for ~20–35s under bursted request fanout; this aligns with the client's observed pauses.
- There's evidence of a keepalive mismatch: client heartbeat is 10s, proxy idle-close is 30s, downstream model container inactivity checks are 25s. Under load, the model container sometimes stalls KV-cache writes briefly which pauses chunk emission.

Hypothesis: timing mismatch combined with a low proxy read-timeout exacerbates transient backend stalls — the proxy aggressively closes the socket, leading to unexpected EOF errors and duplicate reconnects that create a bursty token emission pattern.

Immediate actions (safe, rolling):
1) Change edge proxy websocket idle/read timeout from 30s -> 95s (config flag, no binary deploy).
2) Push an operational heartbeat to clients (10s application-level ping) and document for ClarifyHealth.
3) Enable KV-cache backpressure logging on a narrow sample (5% traffic) to capture stall triggers.
4) Prepare a fallback routing policy to send 30% of traffic to model-variant-rl-202610 (lower memory, more stable under high concurrency).

I'll open INF-1129 and start a 2hr live debug window. ETA for first mitigation (proxy config flip) is ~20 minutes, after which we'll monitor error-rate/median delivery gap.

—Priyom
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@clarityhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clarityhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-22T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream timeouts / production stalls

Diego/Priyom — we are available for the 10:00 PST sync, and confirmed: no model changes on our side this morning. Heartbeat on our client is 10s, as you suspected.

We opted for the fallback variant last week for one of our non-prod clusters; production is on variant-rl-202611 and we've not changed quantization. The business impact: live transcriptions are used mid-encounter; stalls are causing patient/provider call degradation and several reported session drops. We need rapid mitigation and an exec note.

Attaching the pcap; please run the proxy flip and advise.

—Miguel
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream timeouts / production stalls — mitigation update

Update: we applied the proxy websocket idle/read timeout change (30s -> 95s) in us-west rolling across the three edge clusters at 10:28 PST. We also temporarily enabled routing 35% of traffic to model-variant-rl-202610 at 10:35 PST as a safeguard.

Preliminary observations (10:45–11:05 window):
- Error rate on ClarifyHealth streams dropped from 4.9% -> 0.8%.
- Median token delivery gap reduced from 12.4s -> 1.6s for sampled requests.
- No additional unexpected EOF events in the edge logs after the timeout change.

Next steps:
- Keepholding the KV-cache backpressure logs for the 2hr window; if we still see backend stalls we will trace into the model container's memory reclaim behavior and skipping KV writes.
- Prepare exec briefing for 11:30 PST (Lauren to draft, Diego to share) with impact numbers and mitigation timeline.

I'll keep monitoring the metrics and will post another update at 12:30 PST.

—Priyom
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@clarityhealth.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-23T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: ClarifyHealth — executive summary and next steps (post-mitigation)

Miguel / team —

Thanks again for working with us through yesterday's incident. Attached is a one‑page executive summary (exec_briefing_clarity_20261123.pdf) that captures impact, root cause, and our remediation plan. Key points:
- Incident window: 2026-11-22 08:42–11:05 PST.
- Impact: intermittent token-delivery stalls; peak error rate 5.1%, estimated 0.7% of live sessions affected (sustained stalls causing client disconnects).
- Root cause: transient backend KV-cache stalls combined with a conservative edge websocket idle timeout that closed sockets during pause windows, producing unexpected EOF/chunked-transfer failures.
- Actions taken: increased edge websocket idle timeout to 95s (rolled 10:28–10:32 PST), routed 35% traffic to a stable model variant, enabled backpressure logging and longer-term metrics collection.
- Follow-ups: engineering will harden KV-cache write reliability and revisit server-side backpressure handling (INF-1129, target fix in the 2027.01 release).

Short-term asks for ClarifyHealth: document the client-side heartbeat/ping expectations (we recommend 10s application-level pings), and flag any clients not following this pattern so we can make exemptions.

We're committing to a post‑mortem with timeline, RCA, and corrective actions by 2026-11-30. If you'd like a live run-through with your execs, we can set a 30-minute window tomorrow.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
